subject: Banking
title: The Chargeback System
description: A quick, practical guide to The Chargeback System.

hook.text: If your card is used fraudulently, you call your bank and the charge is reversed.

buildup.text: Chargebacks were created by the Fair Credit Billing Act of 1974. They protect consumers from unauthorized charges.

discovery.text: The merchant can dispute chargebacks, but the process is slow, expensive, and heavily favors the cardholder.

twist.text: Friendly fraud is growing. Customers buy products, receive them, then dispute the charge. They keep the item for free.

climax.text: Chargebacks protect consumers but create a system where merchants absorb nearly all payment fraud losses.

punchline.text: Dispute the charge, keep the product. Chargebacks favor buyers.

quiz.question: What is 'friendly fraud' in the chargeback system?
options: Customers disputing legitimate charges to keep products free

details.summary: Chargebacks allow cardholders to dispute transactions and have charges reversed through their issuing bank, providing consumer protection against fraud and merchant disputes but costing merchants billions in lost revenue.
details.whyItMatters: The chargeback system is a cornerstone of consumer trust in card payments but has been heavily abused through friendly fraud. Merchants bear the financial burden of disputes, even when they delivered the product.
takeaways: Consumers can dispute card charges and have them reversed
Merchants lose the sale amount plus a chargeback fee of $20 to $100
Friendly fraud, where consumers falsely claim charges, costs billions

faq.question: What is friendly fraud?
faq.answer: Friendly fraud occurs when a consumer makes a legitimate purchase, receives the product, and then disputes the charge with their bank claiming they never received it or did not authorize it. It costs merchants over $100 billion annually.

faq.question: Can merchants fight chargebacks?
faq.answer: Yes, through the representment process. Merchants can submit evidence proving the transaction was legitimate. However, the process is time-consuming, and banks statistically favor cardholders, so merchants often absorb the loss.
